messages:
nate: FYI getting a handful of Support tickets and alerts showing p95 API latency up ~2x for customers routing through the US-East-1 edge POP. Started ~08:10 UTC. Some TLS handshake timeouts reported too. Any quick visibility?

toni: seeing the same in our edge metrics dashboard — connection_setup p99 spiked from ~40ms to ~220ms around 08:09. No obvious CPU/GPU pressure on frontends.

jess: pulled up the edge LB logs. A bunch of client connections are getting a SIG_TIMEOUT during TLS handshake to backend pools in us-east-1a -> seems like cross-az hop increased. sample log: 
```
[08:11:02] conn_id=7892 accept -> TLS_HANDSHAKE start
[08:11:02] conn_id=7892 backend_connect -> 120ms
[08:11:03] conn_id=7892 TLS_HANDSHAKE timeout (3000ms)
```

sam: i ran a quick traceroute from the affected POP to the backend pool IPs, noticed a hairpin through a transit AS — extra 3 hops compared to normal. Paste: 
```
traceroute to 10.2.5.8 (10.2.5.8), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.1.1  0.5 ms  0.3 ms  0.3 ms
 2  100.64.0.14  1.0 ms  1.1 ms  1.2 ms
 3  203.0.113.12  120.3 ms  121.0 ms  119.9 ms  <-- unexpected transit
 4  10.2.5.8  121.6 ms  120.7 ms  122.0 ms
```

maria: that 203.0.113.12 looks like a cloud provider transitive hop (we usually avoid that path). Could be BGP flapping or a bad anycast fallback. Checking DNS/route changes now.

infra-bot: Edge POP us-east-1 reported increased TLS handshake latency at 2026-03-15T08:09:40Z; related alerts dispatched to eng-infra oncall.

toni: I checked our authoritative DNS for edge->backend SRV records — no changes on our side. But I see increased NXDOMAIN/short TTL resolver activity for the customer-facing edge name from one of our upstream resolvers at ~08:08.

jess: any chance a resolver shift caused clients to hit a different POP with longer path? But tickets are all for clients routed to us-east-1.

sam: i also grabbed tcpdump during the window. Several TCP SYNs retransmitted, then successful but with long RTT before TLS ClientHello. Looks like TCP connect is delayed due to path. snippet: 
```
08:10:58 IP 198.51.100.22.52344 > 10.2.5.8.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
08:11:00 IP 198.51.100.22.52344 > 10.2.5.8.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, length 0 (retransmit)
08:11:02 IP 198.51.100.22.52344 > 10.2.5.8.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, ack 0, length 0
```

nate: sounds like routing/transit hiccup causing TCP/TLS setup delays. Any upstream peering changes logged?

maria: checked BGP update logs — there were a burst of withdrawals and re-announces for the backend cluster prefixes starting 08:07 and resolving around 08:15. ASN 64512 showed flaps. I'll open a ticket with that transit provider.

toni: mitigation suggestion: can we force-route affected POPs to alternate backend anycast set (us-east-2) via immediate policy change? Also consider temporary increasing handshake timeout and enabling shorter client connect retry guidance for support.

jess: we can push policy to steer traffic to us-east-2 by updating edge routing map for the affected customer routes. Doing that will cause brief connection drains — want to coordinate with support and oncall.

support-bot: Opening customer-facing note: "We are investigating increased API latency for some customers in US-East. If you see transient TLS errors, please retry; no changes required on your side." (will update every 30m)

sam: quick repro steps for infra team:
1) curl -v --connect-timeout 2 https://api.redwood.example/health (from us-east-1 POP)
2) if TLS handshake stalls, run `tcptraceroute <backend_ip> 443` and `dig +trace <edge_name>`
3) capture `tcpdump -w /tmp/handoff.pcap port 443` for 2 minutes

nate: jess, please stage the routing change to us-east-2 and I'll coordinate a short maintenance window in #support to inform affected customers. Toni — can you monitor p95/p99 and CPU after change?

jess: staging route update now (will use canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 minutes). Command snippet: 
```
edgectl route-update --pop us-east-1 --target anycast-set=us-east-2 --canary 10 --step 20m
```
toni: watching dashboards. baseline p95 = 110ms, current = 240ms. after canary at 10% => p95 down to 180ms. continuing.

maria: transit provider replied — they saw a partial outage within their backbone at 08:06-08:14 affecting a handful of prefixes, they are doing root-cause with their infra team.

jess: canary -> 50% done. p95 trending down to 130ms. no major error increase.

nate: okay moving to 100% now. updating support note to say mitigated and follow-up will be provided once transit vendor confirms root cause. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Customer note updated: "Mitigation in place — traffic re-routed; latency should be improving. We're tracking with transit provider and will follow up."

sam: saved pcap and traceroutes to /var/log/infra/incidents/1860005432/ for postmortem.

maria: opening provider ticket id TP-8721 and added logs, BGP dumps, and timestamps.

toni: postmortem action items: 1) add more aggressive anycast fallback detection (auto-steer if TLS handshake p99 > 200ms for >2min), 2) add upstream BGP monitoring alerts for withdraws > X/min, 3) playbook update for rerouting policy.

nate: agreed. i'll file the postmortem and link TP-8721. closing thread once postmortem draft is shared.
